environments.title: Environments
environments.subtitle: An environment is what a task's desktop comes with. Everyone on the team can start tasks from these.
environments.empty: No environments. Add one and tasks can start from it.

editor.name: Name
editor.repositorySectionHint: Pick one of your GitHub repositories. If it has a workstream.yml, Workstream fills the settings from it.
editor.findRepositoryPlaceholder: Find one of your repositories by name
editor.noRepositories: Your GitHub account has no repositories yet.
editor.moreRepositories: Only your {count} most recently pushed repositories are listed. For another, type its address.
editor.signInForRepositories: Sign in with GitHub to pick from your repositories. Desktops then push and open pull requests as you.
editor.signInWithGitHub: Sign out and sign in with GitHub
editor.repositoriesFailed: Your repositories could not be read from GitHub. {message}
editor.surfacesHint: Where your product runs. You and the agent see it and use it there.
editor.appsHint: What you and the agent work with. Each one gets a button on the desktop's panel.

sizes.small: Small · 2 cores, 8 GB memory, 64 GB disk
sizes.standard: Standard · 4 cores, 16 GB memory, 64 GB disk
sizes.large: Large · 8 cores, 32 GB memory, 128 GB disk

editor.advancedHint: The setup script, variables and instructions for the agent.
editor.repositoryHint: Cloned when the desktop is made, from any https address. Desktops reach GitHub as the person who started the task.
editor.moreBranches: This repository has more branches than Workstream lists. Type the branch's name.
editor.fromFile: Filled from workstream.yml on {branch}. Each task reads the file again when it starts, so change the file to change these settings.
editor.followsFile: Its settings are workstream.yml in the repository. Each task reads the file again when it starts, so change the file to change these settings.
editor.fileChanged: You changed settings that came from workstream.yml, so this environment no longer follows the file.
editor.badFile: workstream.yml in this repository has mistakes, so nothing was filled from it:
editor.noFile: {repository} has no workstream.yml on {branch}. To keep this environment's settings in the repository, add a file named workstream.yml at its root, like this:
editor.noFileOr: Or fill in the settings below. After you save, you can save them to the repository as workstream.yml.
editor.fileReference: Every setting the file can have
editor.fileOffer: Save these settings as workstream.yml in {repository}, so they live with the code and each task reads them from there.
editor.fileOfferKept: Variable names go in the file; their values stay in Workstream.
editor.saveFile: Save as workstream.yml in the repository
editor.filePullRequest: The branch takes changes only through pull requests, so Workstream opened one from {branch}. Once it is merged, tasks read the file.
editor.setupScriptHint: Runs once on a new desktop, in a terminal you can watch, in the repository's folder when there is one. Use it to install and build. Leave starting the project to the agent: a program the script leaves running stops when the script ends.
editor.variablesHint: Set in every shell on the desktop and given to the agent. Values are stored protected and never shown again.
editor.instructionsHint: Added to what the agent is told on every desktop made from this environment.
editor.instructionsPlaceholder: Run the tests before you say you are done. Leave the app running on port 3000.
editor.deleteBody: Tasks can no longer start from it. Tasks already started from it must be deleted first.

setup.title: Setup
setup.hint: The repository is cloned and the setup script run once, on a desktop of its own, and that desktop is saved. Tasks then start from it with everything in place, and pull the newest commits.
setup.nothing: Nothing to prepare. Add a repository, or a setup script under Advanced.
setup.notPrepared: Not prepared. Each task clones the repository and runs the setup script itself.
setup.waiting: Preparing: waiting for a desktop to prepare it on.
setup.preparedAt: Prepared {when}, at commit {commit}. Tasks start from it.
setup.kept: {gigabytes} GB on its disk, about {cost} a month to keep.
setup.outOfDateSetup: Out of date: the setup changed since it was prepared. Each task runs the setup itself until it is prepared again.
setup.outOfDateDesktop: Out of date: desktops were updated since it was prepared. Each task runs the setup itself until it is prepared again.
setup.failed: The last preparation failed. {failure} Tasks still work: each one runs the setup itself.

team.title: Team
team.subtitle: Everyone on a team can see, use and manage every task and environment in it.
team.name: Team name
team.removeBody: They lose access to this team's tasks and environments at once.
team.leaveBody: You lose access to its tasks and environments.

invite.title: Invite someone
invite.linkBody: Send {email} this link. It works once, and only for that address.
invite.emailedBody: We emailed {email} an invitation. You can also send them this link yourself. It works once, and only for that address.

team.adminOnly: Only an administrator can invite people or change who is on the team.

desktops.title: Desktops
desktops.body: A desktop that nobody is using is paused: its machine is released and its files are kept, and it resumes in about half a minute when someone clicks it or writes to its agent. Use is a person's mouse or keyboard, a message, or the agent working. Having a task open is not. A desktop that stays paused is archived: its disk is saved and its machine deleted, and it comes back in about a minute. Only deleting a task deletes its files.
desktops.pauseAfter: Pause after, in minutes without use
desktops.now: Paused after {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} without use, and archived after {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} paused. An administrator can change this.

email.title: Email
email.taskEmails: Email me when a task I started or wrote in is finished or needs me
email.taskEmailsHint: Not while you have its desktop on screen, and at most once every ten minutes for each task. This is your own setting and applies on every team you are on.

usage.title: Usage
usage.subtitle: What this team has used since {date}.

models.title: Models
models.body: What the team's agents have spent on AI models this month. When the allowance is used up, agents stop until next month or until it is raised.

desktops.title: Desktop time
desktops.empty: No desktop has run this month.
desktops.body: A desktop counts from when it starts until it is paused, and each size is counted on its own. A desktop nobody is using is paused by itself.

storage.title: Storage

about.disk: The disk of each task's desktop, whether the desktop is running or not. Counted at the disk's full size.
about.archive: What is kept of each archived task. Counted at what is on it.
about.setup: Each environment's saved setup, which its tasks start from. Counted at what is on it.

storage.empty: Nothing has been kept this month.
storage.body: A GB‑month is one gigabyte kept for a whole month, so 64 GB kept for half a month is 32 GB‑months. What is kept is counted every 15 minutes.

builds.title: iPhone builds
builds.minutes: {minutes, plural, one {# minute on a Mac} other {# minutes on a Mac}}
builds.body: An iPhone app is built on a Mac, which a desktop asks for when its native code has changed. A change to JavaScript alone uses the build your team already has.
